title: THE ANVIL · MILE REPEATS + THE SQUAT ENGINE
vibe: green · hard on purpose · 60 minutes · the biggest day of the Singapore block
why: Twelve hours of sleep, no soreness, a full rest day behind you, an hour available, and you said HARD. That is the best readiness reading in the log since you got on the plane, and it does not come around often enough to spend carefully. So this is the day the program cashes it in. Two things have gone stale while you were doing other work well: loaded LEG work has not been the main event since the 17th, and you have never once run mile repeats in this program. Today is both, in that order. The run goes FIRST while the legs are fresh, because repeats are a quality session and they deserve your best legs, not your leftovers. Then the squat engine gets what is left. Your shoulders, lats and chest ate four hundred and twenty-six reps on the 20th, so they stay out of the lead entirely today: nothing overhead, nothing pressing. The finisher is a strongman carry medley, which is grip and midline and legs all at once and is the shape of work you have told me twice you like best. Volume is written high because you asked for high and because the last time a session was billed as hard you ran it three times through and it was fine.

blocks.title: WARM-UP · DAY B · ANKLES, KNEES, HIPS
blocks.meta: ~8 min · Moves Method Day B · matched to a leg day · move, do not grind

items.name: TOE SQUAT + ANKLE ROLLS IN THE SQUAT · 90 sec
items.detail: Kneel and sit back on tucked toes for thirty seconds to open the feet and calves. Then drop into a deep squat and roll each ankle through its full circle, driving the knee forward over the toes. You are about to do mile repeats at two hundred and fifty pounds. The ankles get first claim on this warm-up.

items.name: SINGLE-LEG BALANCE + KNEE DRIVES · 90 sec
items.detail: Thirty seconds of balance on each foot, then fifteen driving knee raises per side, tall and controlled. This is the gait wiring and it costs nothing.

items.name: SIDE STEP-UPS + HORSE-STANCE SQUATS · 2 min
items.detail: Ten side step-ups per leg onto a bench or box, then thirty seconds sitting in a wide horse stance, hips low, elbows pushing the knees out. Wakes up the hips laterally, which the squats will want later.

items.name: SINGLE-LEG GOOD MORNING · 8 per side
items.detail: Hands behind the head, hinge on one leg until you feel the hamstring, stand tall. Slow. This is the hinge rehearsal for the swings.

items.name: TREADMILL PRIMER · 3 min
items.detail: Walk 60 seconds at 6 km/h, then jog 2 minutes building from 9 to 12 km/h. Roll straight from the last minute of this into the first repeat. Do not stop the belt and start over.

blocks.text: Day B off the Moves Method menu, which is the ankles-knees-hips day and the correct match for a leg session. Different warm-up from the last three days on purpose.

blocks.title: BLOCK 1 · MILE REPEATS · FIRST TIME IN THIS PROGRAM
blocks.meta: ~18 min · 2 REPEATS of 1.6 km · 3 min walk between · 13.3 to 13.8 km/h
blocks.format: interval repeats at distance, run FRESH, before the weights
blocks.workRest: 1.6 km hard · 3 min walk at 5.5 km/h · repeat

items.name: REPEAT 1 · 1.6 km @ 13.3 km/h
items.detail: Set the belt at 13.3 and hold it for the full 1.6 km. That is roughly a 7:15 mile. It should feel like your two-mile effort but arriving sooner. Expect about 7 minutes 10 seconds. Cadence quick and short, around 168 to 172 steps a minute, which cuts the impact per step without costing you any pace.

items.name: WALK · 3 min @ 5.5 km/h
items.detail: Full three minutes, walking, belt still moving. Do not cut it short because you feel fine. The recovery is what makes the second repeat mean something.

items.name: REPEAT 2 · 1.6 km @ 13.6 to 13.8 km/h
items.detail: Go UP, not down. 13.6 minimum, 13.8 if the first one came easy. That is roughly 7:05 down to 6:58 a mile. A negative split is the whole point of the session and you have run three of them in a row on the two-mile, so this is well inside what you already do.

items.name: IF THE FIRST TWO WERE TOO EASY · REPEAT 3
items.detail: Only if you genuinely have the clock and the legs: take one more 1.6 km at 13.8 or faster after another 3 minute walk. It will cost you the cooldown. Worth it if the day is there.

blocks.text: You have run fartlek, tempo, incline ladders, a one-way climb and a continuous three-miler in this program. You have never run repeats. This is the missing run shape, and it belongs on a fully-rested day at the front of the session where you can actually run it fast. This treadmill reads in km/h and has not been calibrated against your watch yet, so tell me the watch splits afterward and I will pin the conversion.

blocks.title: BLOCK 2 · THE SQUAT ENGINE · GRIND PLUS BALLISTIC
blocks.meta: 20 min running clock · TARGET 8 ROUNDS · stretch 10 · heavy pair of dumbbells + the 20 kg bell
blocks.format: grind + ballistic superset, max quality rounds in 20 minutes
blocks.workRest: 5 front squats, then 15 swings, then rest only as long as you need to keep the squats clean

items.name: A1 · DOUBLE DUMBBELL FRONT SQUAT · 5 reps
items.detail: A pair of dumbbells, roughly 22 to 25 kg each, racked on the shoulders. Pick the heaviest pair you can front squat for five honest reps with the chest up. Sit BETWEEN the ankles, not back. Five reps every round, no more, and they must look the same in round eight as in round one. If they get ugly, drop a size rather than dropping the round count.

items.name: A2 · TWO-HAND SWING · 15 reps · 20 kg
items.detail: Straight off the squats, no set-down break. Fifteen hard swings, hips snapping, bell floating to chest height. The 20 kg is your strength bell now, so these should be sharp and fast, not a grind. Breathe out on every snap.

items.name: THE COUNT
items.detail: EIGHT ROUNDS is the target on the 20 minute clock. That is 40 front squats and 120 swings. TEN ROUNDS is the stretch and would be 50 and 150. Write down what you hit. It sets the load for the rest of the Singapore block.

blocks.noteGreen: Eight rounds minimum. If you finish eight with more than three minutes on the clock, keep going and take ten.
blocks.text: Neupert's Grind and Ballistic pairing, squat plus hinge, which is the exact combination that has been missing since the 17th. Nothing goes overhead in this block. Your pressing muscles are still paying off the 20th and they are not invited.

blocks.title: BLOCK 3 · THE MEDLEY · CARRY IT OR PUT IT DOWN
blocks.meta: ~9 min · 3 LAPS · about 20 metres per station · no set-down inside a lap
blocks.format: strongman medley, measured in distance through space, not in reps
blocks.workRest: one continuous lap through all three carries, then rest 60 to 90 sec, three laps total

items.name: STATION 1 · SUITCASE CARRY · 20 m per side
items.detail: One heavy dumbbell, the heaviest you can hold, hanging at one side. Twenty metres out, switch hands, twenty metres back. Shoulders square, do not lean away from it. This is anti-lateral-flexion core disguised as a walk.

items.name: STATION 2 · ZERCHER CARRY · 20 m · WILDCARD
items.detail: New to this program. Hook a heavy dumbbell or the 20 kg bell into the crooks of both elbows, hugged against the chest, elbows high. Walk twenty metres. The load is out in front of you so your whole midline has to fight to keep you upright, and your upper back has to hold the position. It is uncomfortable and that is the entire point. Straight from the strongman side of the house.

items.name: STATION 3 · FRONT-RACK MARCH · 20 m · 20 kg
items.detail: The 20 kg bell racked on one shoulder, and you march the twenty metres with a deliberate high knee on every step. Switch shoulders for the next lap. Ribs down, do not let the low back arch.

items.name: THE RULE
items.detail: Inside a lap the weight never touches the floor. Grip is the limiter here and grip is supposed to be the limiter. If it goes down, that lap is over, rest, and start the next one.

blocks.text: Three laps. The strongman medley principle: two or more loaded movements back to back, moving weight through space, effort counted in distance instead of reps. Carries and grip work are a confirmed favourite of yours from back on the 15th of July and they have not headlined a finisher since. This also covers the midline requirement without a single crunch.

blocks.title: COOLDOWN · 5 MIN
blocks.meta: walk it off, then get on the floor

items.name: TREADMILL WALK · 2 min @ 5 km/h
items.detail: Flat, easy, nose breathing. Let the heart rate come down before you lie down.

items.name: COUCH STRETCH · 60 sec per side
items.detail: Rear foot elevated, hips square and pushed forward. The quads did the work today and they will be the sore ones tomorrow.

items.name: CALF AND ACHILLES HANG · 45 sec per side
items.detail: Heel dropped off a step. You just ran two hard miles at 250 pounds. Pay the calves back.

items.name: SEATED FORWARD FOLD · 60 sec
items.detail: Legs long, breathe into the hamstrings and low back. Long exhales.

blocks.text: Five minutes. Do not skip the calves today of all days.
